title: Recognition of local ind-etale algebras by geometric neighbourhood colimits
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a commutative local ring with residue field $k$ [def-weil-residue-field], let $K/k$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], and let $\Omega$ be any algebraically closed extension field of $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be induced by $A\to k\hookrightarrow K\hookrightarrow\Omega$. Then the relative separable algebraic closure of $k$ in $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure] is exactly the image of $K$. In every affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,x_V)$ of $x$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], with $v$ the image of $x_V$, the embedding $\kappa(v)\to\Omega$ has image in $K$. Let $C$ be a henselian local commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] such that $A\to C$ is local and ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], with a surjection $q:C\to K$ whose kernel is $\mathfrak m_C$ and whose restriction to $A$ is $A\to k\hookrightarrow K$. Put $G=A^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}A,x}$, the small affine pointed-neighbourhood ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with coprojections $\lambda_V:\Gamma(V)\to G$ and structural map $b:A\to G$. There is exactly one $A$-algebra isomorphism $i:C\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ such that, for every representative $(V,x_V)$, the composite
$$\Gamma(V)\xrightarrow{\lambda_V}G\xrightarrow{i^{-1}}C\xrightarrow{q}K\hookrightarrow\Omega$$
is the map induced by $x_V$. Moreover, let $D_A$ be the ring colimit of the etale residue triples over $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-residue-triples], with coprojections $\mu_t:B_t\to D_A$ and induced residue map $q_A:D_A\to K$. For a representative $(V,x_V)$, with $v$ the image of $x_V$, $\mathfrak q_v\subset\Gamma(V)$ its prime and $\phi_v:\kappa(\mathfrak q_v)\to K$ the residue embedding given by $x_V$, put $t_V=(\Gamma(V),\mathfrak q_v,\phi_v)$, with structure map the chart map $A\to\Gamma(V)$; it is an etale residue triple. There is exactly one ring map $g:D_A\to G$ with $g\circ\mu_{t_V}=\lambda_V$ for every representative $(V,x_V)$; it is an $A$-algebra isomorphism and $q\circ i^{-1}\circ g=q_A$. The assertion holds without any perfectness assumption on $k$, and is independent of the chosen small representative category. There exists an algebraic closure of $K$, and any such closure is an allowed choice of $\Omega$.

proof.text: For a separable element z over k, tower_top makes z separable over K. A separably closed field has no nontrivial separable subextension, so z is in the image of K. Conversely separability of K/k maps through the tower. This is the complete Mathlib argument in the Lean proof.

Apply geometric_triples_diagram_comparison. It supplies residue containment, representing triples, b, and g with inverse, structural equations, evaluation formula and uniqueness, for the arbitrary small representative equivalence r.

Put rho=b followed by inverse g; triple structural equations give its coprojection formula. Apply geometric_triples_algebra_recognition to obtain e:C ~= c.pt, preserving A and the residue map, together with uniqueness of inverse maps.

Set i=e followed by g. Its base and point equations follow from the structural and residue equations. For another i prime, compare its inverse composed with q and K -> Omega with inverse g composed with qA and K -> Omega. On every geometric coprojection both are evaluation, so colimit hom_ext makes them equal. Injectivity of K -> Omega implies q composed with inverse i prime composed with g equals qA. This inverse composite also preserves A; algebraic recognition uniqueness identifies it with inverse e. Surjectivity of g now identifies inverse i prime with inverse i, hence i prime=i. Cancelling g with its inverse gives q inverse i g=qA, and diagram comparison supplies uniqueness of g.
Choose AlgebraicClosure K with its Field, Algebra and IsAlgClosure instances.
